items.text: Mississippi has a medical cannabis program run by the State Department of Health; there is no adult-use cannabis. Visitors who medically qualify and hold an active medical card from their home state can apply for a Mississippi non-resident card up to 30 days before arriving; it is valid for 15 days and only in Mississippi. Non-resident cardholders may possess up to 14 MMCEUs (the state's measuring unit for medical cannabis) and buy up to 6 a week and 12 in any 15 days. The law doesn't allow use in a public place or in a motor vehicle.

laws.rule: Medical cannabis is legal in Mississippi for approved medical use only; recreational use and possession remain illegal. Outside the medical program, possessing up to 30 grams is a civil offence (a first offence carries a US$250 fine, about A$355), a second offence may bring the fine plus five to 60 days in jail, and later offences up to US$1,000 and five days to six months. More than 30 grams is a felony (30 to 250 grams: one to three years in prison and up to US$1,000). The state's toolkit sets purchase limits for non-resident (visitor) cardholders at 6 units in 7 days and 12 units in 15 days (1 unit is 3.5 grams of flower); how a visitor becomes a cardholder was not read. Cannabis also stays illegal under US federal law, including on federal land. US$ rates: A$1 = USD 0.7040 (RBA, 30 Oct 2026), so US$1 is about A$1.42.
laws.penalty_signal: First offence up to 30 g: US$250 civil fine; over 30 g: felony

laws.rule: Having cannabis in any part of a motor vehicle other than the trunk is a misdemeanour, with a fine up to US$1,000 (about A$1,420) and up to 90 days in jail. Smoking or vaping medical cannabis in public places or inside a motor vehicle is prohibited, and so is driving, boating or flying under its influence. Home growing is not permitted.
